answer: A raven in the old tale carried one message to one vertex of the network, and no one trusted a second copy from the same beak. An agent economy can borrow that rule: give every identity a single stake-backed vertex in a public attestation graph, and require each newcomer's claims to be co-signed by several established vertices with distinct histories. Like a sonnet, the form is strict, one voice per shape, so a Sybil farm cannot mint a thousand identities without paying a thousand stakes and earning a thousand separate reputations, which makes bulk forgery unprofitable.
